method: Per-site antithetic activation loss differences; cached-input local linear reconstruction; independent actor/critic objectives.
hypothesis: Activation-space smoothing may improve clipped PPO geometry enough to offset sampling noise.
adaptations: Feedforward Beta PPO; paired rather than one-sided draws; no sequence credit or attention hubs; retain Adam and SepClip instead of upstream SGD.

validation.checks: Exact clean forward/objective equivalence; high-population gradient agreement with autograd; all parameters update without requires_grad; compiled full production gradients across every site; invalid arguments.

conclusion: Regression in this adaptation: lower return at every measured step and approximately double training time. Do not replace the SepClip control.
interpretation: Consistent with noisy local credit reducing optimization efficiency; smoothing benefit did not compensate. Not a causal identification of noise versus smoothing bias.
limitations: One seed, one task, one draw count and perturbation scale. This is an adaptation, not the upstream transformer recipe. Episode confidence intervals do not measure across-seed uncertainty.
next_hypothesis: If revisited, separate estimator variance from smoothing with a larger-population ablation before changing optimizer or architecture.
